newsletter.markdown:
1. **Discovery & Translational Science**

* **Peripheral axonopathy identified as critical limitation of microdystrophin gene therapy in DMD** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.17.744857)
  * Single-nucleus RNA sequencing and structural analyses in *mdx* mouse models demonstrated that Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) involves active peripheral nerve denervation and impaired neural repair pathways independent of muscle necrosis.
  * Full-length dystrophin (Dp427c) is normally expressed in peripheral nerves at Schmidt-Lanterman incisures and Nodes of Ranvier; its absence causes localized structural collapse.
  * Muscle-restricted microdystrophin gene therapy preserved sarcolemmal integrity but failed to restore nerve-muscle connectivity or resolve neurotransmission defects, establishing DMD as a dual motor unit pathology.

* **Iatrogenic transmission risk of amyloid β pathology via blood products evaluated** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)00767-1/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * Clinical evidence of iatrogenic cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA) and Alzheimer disease following historic medical procedures suggests that seeded protein misfolding and aggregation of amyloid β could pose a risk of transmission through transfused blood components.

* **Machine learning framework optimizes short-form perinatal depression screening** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.10.13.25337771)
  * Validation across National Clinical Cohort Collaborative data (n = 22,924) showed that 2-question subsets of the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (Q4+Q8 or Q5+Q8) predicted full 10-item scores with an R² = 0.70.
  * Binary classification modeling maintained diagnostic accuracy at standard clinical thresholds (score ≥ 13), offering reduced administration time in clinical workflows.

* **Quantitative accounting model establishes energetic requirements for human muscle synthesis** [bioRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.17.745156)
  * A bottom-up accounting model integrating tissue composition, synthesis costs, and diet-induced thermogenesis calculated a central physiological deposition requirement of 10,830 kJ/kg for skeletal muscle accretion.
  * Including resting maintenance and thermogenesis yielded a total metabolizable energy intake requirement of 14,570 kJ/kg (~3,481 kcal/kg) of wet muscle mass.

2. **Early Trials — Phase I–II**

* **Off-the-shelf mutant KRAS vaccine induces durable T-cell responses in high-risk pancreatic cancer cohort** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/d41591-026-00041-3)
  * A Phase 1 study of an off-the-shelf vaccine targeting mutant KRAS showed a favorable safety profile and successfully elicited durable T-cell immune responses in healthy individuals at high risk for pancreatic cancer.

3. **Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III**

* **[Biotech]** **Moderna and Merck report Phase 3 success for individualized mRNA cancer vaccine intismeran in melanoma** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/moderna-merck-intismeran-melanoma-vaccine-stock-reaction/828332/)
  * Moderna and Merck announced that their individualized mRNA neoantigen vaccine, intismeran, administered with Keytruda, met its primary endpoint in a pivotal Phase 3 melanoma study.
  * Market capitalization for Moderna increased significantly following the announcement, with sell-side analysts raising price targets based on peak sales potential across multiple oncology indications.
  * Equity analysts noted market expectations currently reflect >$20B in peak risk-adjusted sales for the program [X / @BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2090387063057125713).

* **[Big Pharma]** **TALENTOP trial demonstrates benefit of liver resection following atezolizumab and bevacizumab in advanced HCC** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01252-3/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * Results from the randomized Phase 3 TALENTOP trial in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with macrovascular invasion demonstrated that surgical liver resection following systemic atezolizumab plus bevacizumab significantly extended time to treatment failure compared with continued maintenance therapy.

* **Long-term HOST-EXAM follow-up supports clopidogrel over aspirin monotherapy post-PCI** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01206-7/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * A 10-year follow-up of the randomized HOST-EXAM trial confirmed sustained reductions in composite ischemic and bleeding outcomes for clopidogrel monotherapy versus aspirin monotherapy after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), without an adverse mortality signal.

* **KRYSTAL-12 trial data contextualizes patient-reported outcomes for adagrasib** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01198-0/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * Trial updates from KRYSTAL-12 in KRAS-G12C–mutated non-small-cell lung cancer noted that overall health utility (EQ-5D-5L) scores remained comparable between treatment groups despite a higher incidence of gastrointestinal adverse events in the adagrasib arm.

* **Extended J-START trial analysis quantifies long-term impact of adjunctive ultrasound in breast screening** [The Lancet](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)00930-X/fulltext?rss=yes)
  * Long-term follow-up (180 months) of the J-START trial indicated that adding ultrasonography to mammography in women aged 40–49 led to a small absolute reduction in stage ≥ 2 breast cancer incidence (1.08% vs 1.14%), though overall breast cancer mortality remained unchanged (21 deaths per group).

4. **Regulatory & Approvals**

* **[Biotech]** **FDA approves Ultragenyx's Glenglycos as first gene therapy for GSDIa** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/ultragenyx-fda-approve-genglycos-GSDIa-gene-therapy/828369/)
  * The FDA cleared Glenglycos, an AAV-based single-dose gene therapy designed to deliver a functional gene to the liver to address metabolic imbalance in glycogen storage disease type Ia (GSDIa).
  * Ultragenyx established a wholesale acquisition cost of $2.7M per patient and received a Priority Review Voucher (PRV) upon approval.

* **[Big Pharma]** **FDA approves Regeneron's Pasatru (garetosmab) for rare bone condition FOP** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/regeneron-pasatru-fda-approve-fibrodysplasia-ossificans-progressiva/828375/)
  * Regeneron received FDA approval for Pasatru (garetosmab), an anti-Activin A monoclonal antibody indicated for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP).
  * Approval was supported by Phase 3 data demonstrating a ≥ 90% reduction in new heterotopic ossification compared to placebo over one year; annual list pricing is expected to range between $693,000 and $2.1M based on weight-based dosing (3 or 10 mg/kg).

* **[Biotech]** **Capricor Therapeutics attempts to avert FDA rejection for deramiocel in DMD** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/20/capricor-therapeutics-duchenne-treatment-fda/)
  * Capricor Therapeutics is engaging with regulatory authorities to address deficiencies and avoid a formal rejection of its cell therapy candidate, deramiocel, for Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

* **Optimal Balance Pharmacy recalls compounded glutathione due to endotoxin levels** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/safety/recalls-market-withdrawals-safety-alerts/optimal-balance-pharmacy-issues-voluntary-nationwide-recall-certain-lots-compounded-glutathione-200)
  * Optimal Balance Pharmacy initiated a voluntary nationwide recall of one lot of compounded Glutathione Injection (200 mg/mL, 30 mL multi-dose vials) after internal testing revealed elevated bacterial endotoxin levels.

5. **Business & Strategy**

* **[Biotech]** **Fractyl Health plans commercial strategy update for Revita in post-GLP-1 maintenance** [X / @BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2090394386743931128)
  * Fractyl Health scheduled a Virtual Commercial Strategy Day for Sept 1 to outline clinical and commercial development plans for Revita, a procedural therapy targeting weight maintenance following GLP-1 withdrawal.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Merck downgraded by Wall Street on upcoming Keytruda patent expiry** [X / @BioStocks](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2090399775988273535)
  * RBC downgraded Merck ($MRK) to Sector Perform, pointing to elevated valuation multiples relative to modest near-term growth and loss of exclusivity for Keytruda within two years.

6. **Public Health & Policy**

* **School-level surveillance analysis reveals unmonitored measles transmission risks** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04612-2)
  * A nationwide evaluation of vaccination records from >50,000 US schools found that school-level transmission risk crossed the epidemic threshold 2–3 years prior to recent outbreaks, whereas aggregated county-level metrics remained consistently below threshold levels.

* **Causal model ties white-tailed deer population growth to self-reported Alpha-gal syndrome** [medRxiv](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.08.13.26360354)
  * Using a causal framework applied to citizen-science observation data, researchers linked increased white-tailed deer sightings to higher county-level presence of *Amblyomma americanum* ticks and subsequent self-reported Alpha-gal syndrome cases.

* **US FDA leadership transitions proceed following commissioner nomination** [STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/20/heidi-overton-fda-commissioner-nominee-erica-schwartz-cdc-speech/)
  * Background details emerged following the official nomination of Heidi Overton as FDA Commissioner, alongside initial strategic addresses to CDC staff by leadership.

***

**Worth watching:** Moderna and Merck's Phase 3 success for intismeran represents the first pivotal validation of a custom mRNA neoantigen vaccine in solid tumors, but translational findings showing microdystrophin gene therapy fails to fix peripheral nerve collapse in DMD highlight structural hurdles for gene therapies in neuromuscular disease.

youtube.markdown:
- Biology & Health
    - [Only One Type of Coffee Protects against Dementia - Why?](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gy0FW6xj21o) -- Physionic
        - Analyzes the specific biochemical mechanisms through which coffee consumption may provide protective effects against dementia.
        - Examines the relationship between adenosine receptor modulation and amyloid toxicity in neural tissues.
        - Covers mechanisms involved in amyloid clearance as well as the optimal coffee dosage relative to tau pathology.
    - [Mental health and the price of modernity | Linus Abrams, M.D.](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/Essbq01Xb1E) -- Peter Attia MD
        - Discusses estradiol's role as a key brain hormone regulating multiple neurotransmitter systems across both men and women.
        - Highlights the importance of differentiating bipolar disorder from ordinary depression and how the menopause transition can reveal previously undiagnosed cases.
        - Identifies chronically elevated cortisol as a major underlying driver of modern mental health struggles that remains difficult to treat directly.
        - Explores the evolutionary mismatch between modern environments and human biological design as a key factor in rising anxiety and depression rates.
- Pure Science
    - [Are We Thinking Correctly About AI Intelligence? | PODCAST: The Joy of Why](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cSZo8GZIUYI) -- Quanta Magazine
        - Computer scientist Melanie Mitchell conceptualizes AI as a form of "alien intelligence" that processes information using non-human cognitive mechanisms rather than true human reasoning.
        - Proposes adapting cognitive assessment methodologies from developmental and animal psychology to measure machine cognition, outlining six foundational evaluation principles.
        - Addresses methodological pitfalls in AI testing, including spurious cues (the "Clever Hans" effect), task-centric evaluation constraints, and the gap between competence and performance.
        - Discusses mechanistic interpretability and transfer learning challenges in AI, including AI-assisted breakthroughs in mathematics.
- Other
    - [The Mystery Behind Earth’s Missing Rocks: Crash Course Geology #16](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZLc9udbCaeI) -- CrashCourse
        - Explores how geologists interpret Earth's history through the analysis of sedimentary strata and rock layers, using the Grand Canyon as a primary model.
        - Investigates the geological phenomenon responsible for over one billion years of missing rock layers in the rock record.
        - Explains the concept of unconformities and outlines the leading geological theories that account for these massive gaps in time.
- To watch
